analysis: This PR adds Gemma 4 routed-expert metadata and a test, plus a docs index entry. Examined the following. (1) Gemma4StageGeometry.swift: extracts the constants routedExperts=128 and expertsPerToken=8 (lines 13-14) and reuses them in the strict config validation at lines 49-50. The values are identical to the previous literals, so validation of the num_experts and top_k_experts config fields is unchanged. (2) Gemma4PlacementFamily.swift lines 88-96: adds the expertRouting property and isRoutedExpert(storedTensor:). The latter is a pure string test on a tensor name: a layer index must parse and the name must contain '.experts.switch_glu.'. It is metadata-only and handles no keys, plaintext, attestation or network input. The risk is placement and hardware-prior accuracy: an expert-bytes undercount could bias capacity or decode-cost estimates. The inventory fingerprint check (requireRegisteredInventory, lines 122-128) still pins tensor names, dtype, shape and bytes to the registered artifact, which bounds attacker influence on the naming. Whether the consuming planner (outside the supplied evidence) handles routing and loadedBytes safely, for example with no divide-by-zero or overflow, could not be verified. (3) GemmaRoutedExpertChecks.swift is a test-only addition that reads retained header fixtures and asserts golden layouts and byte counts. It has no production attack surface. (4) docs/reports/README.md adds one index link and a date bump; docs only. No changes touch the coordinator-provider WebSocket, E2E encryption, App Attest, prefix cache or fan helper. No threat-model assets (A-001..A-019) or boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011, TB-012, TB-013) are affected. Remaining open question: the cluster placement and hardware-prior code consuming ClusterExpertRouting was not supplied.
